subject: tiger beetle
title: This Beetle Runs So Fast It Goes Blind Mid-Chase

scenes.text: This beetle runs so fast that it cannot see where it is going.
The tiger beetle covers about 120 of its body lengths every single second.
For a human, that would mean running about 480 miles an hour.
But its eyes can't collect enough light at that speed. The world blurs into a smear.
So it sprints, stops, looks around to find its prey, then sprints again.
It is blind for most of the chase and still catches dinner. Speed beats sight.

description:
Tiger beetles can cover about 120 body lengths a second, so fast that their eyes can't gather enough light to see.
They solve it by stopping three or four times during a chase to relocate their prey.
Would you rather run that fast blind or walk and see? Comment below.
thumbnail_text: IT RUNS SO FAST IT GOES BLIND
first_comment: The fastest beetles top out around 5 miles an hour, which sounds slow until you scale it to their size. What is the fastest animal you have ever seen?
